task.description: Run WF-02 Step 3's scope test first, then produce test specs and test code for REQ-023. ORCH's expectation, which you should re-derive rather than assume: the scope test is YES -- this requirement shipped six real Ecto.Schema modules with changesets and validations, six migrations with a load-bearing conditional guard, and a materially changed tenant_scoped_migrations/0. That is genuine application-executable surface, not the docs-only or build-config-only case the scope test exists to skip. Four explicit carry-forward instructions from the two hard gates that already passed are listed in the dispatch prompt and must not be dropped.
acceptance_criteria: the WF-02 Step 3 scope test is run first and its verdict stated with reasoning
every one of REQ-023's 5 acceptance criteria has at least one runnable test that would fail if the criterion were violated
test specs are written under test/specs/ alongside the test code, not as an afterthought
no test depends on wall-clock time or unseeded randomness
test fixtures use per-test unique data; no cross-test pollution, no shared hardcoded IDs
the section-4 prefix() guard test and the manifest version-to-filename consistency assertion are both written
the two stale statements ISS-0017 identified are refreshed

result.summary:
SCOPE TEST (run first, re-derived from the artefacts, not inherited): YES -- REQ-023 produced substantial application-executable surface. lib/letflow/event_store/ ships six Ecto.Schema modules with composite/natural primary keys, an Ecto.Enum field, a read_after_writes field and seven changeset functions carrying validate_required/validate_length/validate_number/unique_constraint/foreign_key_constraint; the six migrations each contain a load-bearing `if prefix() do` conditional whose two branches produce materially different database state (control flow, not a declaration); and tenant_scoped_migrations/0 changed from returning [] to returning six entries plus a Code.ensure_loaded?-guarded Code.require_file side effect, and now drives real DDL as replay_migrations/2's default migration_source. Nothing here is in the mix.exs/.formatter.exs/config-declaration category the scope test exists to skip. Steps 3b and 4 proceed normally.

ARTEFACTS: test/specs/REQ-023.md (20 numbered test cases, each with a 'why it exists' rationale rather than a restatement of the criterion), test/letflow/event_store/schemas_test.exs (24 pure no-I/O tests, async: true) and test/letflow/event_store/migrations_test.exs (13 integration tests against real Postgres via REQ-022's provision-then-replay, async: false).

ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION -> TEST MAPPING (all 5 covered by runnable tests that fail if violated):
AC1 (six migrations apply cleanly against a provisioned tenant schema via REQ-022's replay, all using :prefix) -> migrations_test.exs 'replay_migrations/2 applies every registered tenant-scoped migration and all six event-store tables land in the tenant's own schema, never in public' (asserts applied version list == the registered manifest, asserts each of the six tables exists under the tenant schema AND refutes its presence in public -- the refute half is what proves :prefix is doing the work -- and asserts Registration.migrations_applied_at was stamped); 'each event-store table's real column set in the tenant schema matches its Ecto.Schema module's field list exactly' (equality, not subset, across all six tables: information_schema.columns vs __schema__(:fields)); 'tenant_scoped_migrations/0 registers all six REQ-023 event-store migrations' (the registration half of design section 4's two mandatory halves).
AC2 (events' PK is (event_id, created_at), not a bare event_id) -> migrations_test.exs 'events' physical primary key in the tenant schema is (event_id, created_at), in that order, not a bare event_id' (ordered PK columns from information_schema; order asserted because (created_at, event_id) would pass a set-equality check while being the wrong shape for the partitioning retrofit) + 'events_archive carries the same composite primary key'; schemas_test.exs 'Event's primary key is the composite (event_id, created_at), not a bare event_id' and 'neither primary-key component is autogenerated (design INV-EV-5)'. Both the DB and schema-module halves are pinned because a correct migration plus an incorrect schema module is a real silent failure mode.
AC3 (no update_changeset/2 or any UPDATE path on events; moduledoc states the immutability invariant per 0003 Decision C point 1) -> schemas_test.exs 'Event's own public API is exactly insert_changeset/2 -- no update_changeset/2, no generic changeset/2, no other update path'. Per the dispatch instruction this is the STRUCTURAL assertion and is written as an exact-set equality over Event.__info__(:functions) (with Ecto's __-prefixed generated functions filtered out), not a deny-list of the two names the criterion happens to mention -- only an exact set covers the criterion's 'or any function that issues an UPDATE' clause, so a future revise_changeset/2 or touch/1 fails too. Paired with 'the four other append-only event-store schemas likewise expose only insert_changeset/2' and, critically, the negative control 'InstanceProjection deliberately DOES expose update_changeset/2 -- the contrast that proves the two tests above discriminate', which prevents the whole group from being vacuously true. The moduledoc half is 'Event's moduledoc states the append-only immutability invariant and cites 0003 Decision C point 1', read via Code.fetch_docs/1 (compiled Docs chunk) as instructed, never by reading the .ex file as a string.
AC4 (unique index on idempotency_key; moduledoc states it supersedes event_store.md Open Question #1) -> migrations_test.exs 'the idempotency sidecar carries a real unique index on idempotency_key' (via pg_indexes, NOT information_schema.table_constraints -- Ecto's create unique_index emits CREATE UNIQUE INDEX rather than ADD CONSTRAINT UNIQUE, so a test written against the constraint views would pass vacuously); 'neither events nor events_archive carries a unique index on idempotency_key -- the sidecar is the single enforcement point' (the executable form of the word 'supersedes', and design INV-EV-3); 'a second row claiming the same idempotency_key is rejected by uq_event_idempotency_key' (behavioural, through the real insert_changeset with :prefix threaded, pinning the {:error, changeset} shape so a name drift surfacing as Ecto.ConstraintError is caught); schemas_test.exs 'IdempotencyRecord's moduledoc states it supersedes event_store.md's Open Question #1 two-phase check' and 'IdempotencyRecord.insert_changeset/2 declares the uq_event_idempotency_key unique constraint by name'.
AC5 (instance_projections moduledoc states schema is event-store scope, population is EE-01/S3 scope) -> schemas_test.exs 'InstanceProjection's moduledoc scopes the schema to the event store and its population to EE-01/S3' (all three load-bearing sentences, not one keyword). This is the one criterion with no stronger structural fact available -- 'this table's population is somebody else's job' is not expressible as a column constraint -- so the doc assertion is primary here rather than the weaker half of a pair, and it is used only because the criterion explicitly demands that text. Its nearest structural guard is migrations_test.exs's exact column-set equality, which fails if S3's engine-owned columns ever leak into this migration and quietly falsify the moduledoc claim; plus 'instance_projections and instance_sequence use instance_id as their natural primary key' and 'terminal?/1 is true for :completed and :cancelled only -- :error is NOT terminal' (status set enumerated from Ecto.Enum.values/2, not hand-listed, so a future fifth status forces a deliberate decision).

FOUR CARRY-FORWARD INSTRUCTIONS -- all four handled:
(1) SECTION 4 GUARD TEST -- WRITTEN, and empirically proven load-bearing. migrations_test.exs 'every migration registered in tenant_scoped_migrations/0 creates nothing in public when run with no :prefix (§4 guard pattern)' iterates the real manifest and runs each registered module through Ecto.Migrator.run/4 with NO :prefix option at all (the exact shape of a plain mix ecto.migrate bootstrap), each under a synthetic never-before-applied probe version (990_000_000 + System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic])) so Migrator genuinely executes change/0 instead of skipping it as already-applied -- reusing the real versions would have made the test pass vacuously, since they are already in public.schema_migrations. It asserts the returned version list (proving the migration RAN) and then asserts public's table set is identical to a snapshot taken before the run. It also refutes an empty manifest, so it can never silently revert to the vacuous state it was in during REQ-022. MUTATION-VERIFIED, not asserted: I temporarily removed the `if prefix() do ... end` guard from priv/repo/migrations/20260816120002_create_instance_sequence.exs and re-ran -- exactly this one test failed (12/13 passed) with 'a registered tenant-scoped migration created something in public when run with no :prefix', no other test's status changed, and the defensive stray-cleanup correctly fired (DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "public"."instance_sequence" CASCADE). The mutation was reverted with git checkout --; `git diff --stat -- priv/repo/migrations/` is empty and the file is byte-identical to the committed version; 13/13 passed again afterwards.
(2) MANIFEST VERSION-TO-FILENAME CONSISTENCY -- WRITTEN. migrations_test.exs 'each registered migration's version matches the numeric prefix of the file it was actually loaded from' reads module_info(:compile)[:source] -- the path the module was ACTUALLY loaded from, which is the load-bearing structural fact rather than a re-derivation of the naming convention -- and asserts its basename equals "<version>_<underscored module suffix>.exs", that Code.ensure_loaded?(module) is true (which is what catches a manifest filename element pointing at a file that does not define that module), and that the file exists in the priv directory tenant_scoped_migrations/0 itself resolves (Application.app_dir(:letflow, "priv")). Compared by basename deliberately: the loading path differs between mix ecto.migrate's in-VM compile (project priv/) and Code.require_file (_build copy), while the basename is identical in both. Paired with 'registered migration versions are unique and strictly ascending', matching the manifest's own documented ordering contract.
(3) TWO STALE STATEMENTS -- BOTH REFRESHED. test/support/req022_migration_fixture.ex's moduledoc (was: "tenant_scoped_migrations/0 is [] at this point in the project's history") now reads "at REQ-022's time tenant_scoped_migrations/0 returned []" plus a '**Refreshed by REQ-023 (ISS-0017).**' paragraph stating it now returns six entries, why the fixture is deliberately kept anyway (it is the one guard-pattern-following migration deliberately OUTSIDE the production manifest, keeping REQ-022's coverage independent of that manifest's contents), and a pointer to the new guard test. test/specs/REQ-022.md:286 (was: "tenant_scoped_migrations/0 itself returns [] today ... there is nothing in that list yet to iterate over") now reads "returned [] at the time this test was written ... there was nothing in that list yet to iterate over", with a '**Refreshed by REQ-023 (ISS-0017).**' paragraph naming the new test that does the full iteration REVIEWER originally asked for. lib/letflow/design/req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md was NOT touched, exactly as instructed -- confirmed by `git status` showing no change under lib/.
(4) TWO DO-NOTS -- BOTH RESPECTED. The six migration files were NOT reformatted; `git diff --stat -- priv/repo/migrations/` is empty and the project-wide `mix format --check-formatted` gate exits 0 unchanged (verified: 'FORMAT GATE EXIT 0'). event_payload_store's on_delete: :restrict was NOT changed to CASCADE; instead migrations_test.exs 'deleting an events row that has an event_payload_store row is blocked by ON DELETE RESTRICT (design OQ-2's deliberate signal)' ASSERTS the restrict behaviour (assert_raise Ecto.ConstraintError, then confirms the event row survives), so a future well-meaning flip to :delete_all fails here loudly rather than being discovered as data loss in REQ-026. Inserting the payload row with the event's own (event_id, created_at) pair also proves both columns of the composite FK are wired.

REAL TEST OUTPUT (quoted, No Speculation):
- Baseline before my work, `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test --seed 0`: "Finished in 1.4 seconds (0.8s async, 0.6s sync)" / "Result: 161 passed (4 properties, 157 tests)" -- matches the 161/161 baseline stated in the dispatch.
- New pure file alone, `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/event_store/schemas_test.exs --seed 0`: "Finished in 0.4 seconds (0.4s async, 0.00s sync)" / "Result: 24 passed".
- New integration file alone, `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/event_store/migrations_test.exs --seed 0`: "Finished in 5.3 seconds (0.00s async, 5.3s sync)" / "Result: 13 passed".
- Full suite after my work, `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test --seed 0`: "Finished in 7.3 seconds (0.8s async, 6.4s sync)" / "Result: 198 passed (4 properties, 194 tests)". 161 -> 198 is exactly the 37 tests I added (24 + 13); zero failures, zero regressions.
- Project format gate, `mix format --check-formatted`: exits 0 (unchanged; the six migrations were left alone per instruction 4).
- ISS-0011 (GitHub #65), reported accurately and NOT fixed: across six unpinned-seed runs of the full suite, five were clean at 198 passed and one (seed 854940) produced "Result: 197/198 passed (4/4 properties, 193/194 tests)" with the single failure being "1) test method short-circuit -- no DB query at all for a non-write method a GET request issues no Ecto query at all (method short-circuit, no DB round-trip) (Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatusTest) / test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs:121". That is exactly the pre-existing flake the dispatch named. None of my 37 tests failed in any run, at any seed.
- Cleanup verified empirically after the runs, against letflow_test2: orphan tenant schemas [], stray probe versions in public.schema_migrations [], leftover public.tenant_schemas rows 0, leftover req022-/req023- test tenants 0, and public's table list byte-identical to before my work (approvals, groups, schema_migrations, tenant_role, tenant_schemas, tenants, transition_events, users). No event-store table leaked into public.

TEST QUALITY RULES (Step 3b's gate): no test reads a clock -- every timestamp used as data is the fixed literal ~U[2026-01-02 03:04:05.000000Z], and the only real-clock value asserted on is Registration.migrations_applied_at, matched merely as %NaiveDateTime{} (was stamped), never a value. No unseeded randomness -- per-test uniqueness comes from Ecto.UUID.generate/0 and System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic]) (a VM counter, not an RNG), the two mechanisms identity_test.exs and tenant_provisioning_test.exs already use; no :rand, no hand-rolled seed. Per-test unique fixtures -- each DB test provisions its own tenant, its own tenant_<32 hex> physical schema and its own Registration row; no shared hardcoded IDs. Every created schema is dropped in on_exit (DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE plus its tenant_schemas and tenants rows), because these tests genuinely commit under Sandbox :auto mode. The guard block's stray-table cleanup is doubly safe: it drops a public table only if the name is one of the six event-store names AND it was absent from the snapshot taken before that test ran, so it can never destroy pre-existing state. All tests are self-sufficient; none reads state another test wrote. No hardcoded secrets, hostnames, ports or connection strings. No @tag :skip and no 'TODO: implement test' anywhere. On ISS-0011 specifically: schemas_test.exs is async: true but attaches NO global :telemetry handler and does zero DB I/O (module metadata and Code.fetch_docs/1 only), and migrations_test.exs -- which creates real schemas -- is async: false, so no second instance of ISS-0011's mistake was introduced.

issues.description: NEW FINDING (not one of ISS-0012..ISS-0020, not filed by me per instruction): REQ-023's own design artefact lib/letflow/design/req023-event-store-schema.md now carries the same class of stale statement ISS-0017 was filed about for the REQ-022 design doc. Line 46 says tenant_scoped_migrations/0 '(196-198, currently returns [])' and line 883 says 'tenant_scoped_migrations/0 currently returns []'. Both were accurate when CODE-DESIGNER wrote them at Step 1 and both were falsified by this run's own Step 2a, which registered six entries. I did not edit the file: it is a gated design artefact that passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, and it is outside my owned_modules. Suggest folding this into ISS-0017 (#73) alongside the req022 design doc's line 407, since it is the identical defect shape and would otherwise be found again by the next agent that greps for it.

ENVIRONMENTAL, observed while working, not a defect in this run's code: Letflow.Application hardcodes the Bandit listener to port 4000 (lib/letflow/application.ex:25), and MIX_TEST_PARTITION only partitions the DATABASE (config/test.exs line 6), not the port. One `mix run`/`mix test` invocation in this worktree aborted with ':eaddrinuse ... port 4000 already in use' while the sibling worktree held it, and it succeeded on retry. This means two worktrees cannot run the suite concurrently even though the DB partitioning was designed to let them. Not filed by me; raising it so ORCH can decide whether it warrants its own issue, since it will bite any future parallel two-worktree run. Note also that MIX_TEST_PARTITION only takes effect under MIX_ENV=test: a bare `mix run` ignores it and targets letflow_dev, which is worth stating explicitly wherever the partition convention is documented.
